name: Adonijah
bio:
Adonijah was David's son by Haggith, born after Absalom and now, with Amnon and Absalom both dead, the eldest surviving heir to the throne. As David grew old and feeble, Adonijah set himself up as king, gathering chariots, horsemen, and fifty men to run ahead of him, encouraged by a father who had never once corrected him, "Why do you behave as you do?" He won the support of Joab and the priest Abiathar, and held a lavish sacrificial feast at En Rogel, inviting all his royal brothers except Solomon and all the royal officials except Nathan, Benaiah, and David's elite guard (1 Kings 1:5-10).

Warned by the prophet Nathan, Bathsheba went to David and reminded him of his oath that Solomon would reign after him; Nathan then confirmed her account, and David swore on the spot that Solomon would be made king that very day. Solomon was anointed at Gihon by Zadok and Nathan amid great public rejoicing, and when news of it reached Adonijah's feast, his guests scattered in fear and Adonijah himself fled to the altar, grasping its horns for sanctuary until Solomon promised to spare him if he proved himself worthy (1 Kings 1:11-53).

After David's death, Adonijah came to Bathsheba and asked her to request that Solomon give him Abishag, the young woman who had cared for David in his old age, as his wife. Solomon read the request as a renewed challenge for the throne itself — since taking a former king's concubine could be read as a claim to his crown — and had Benaiah strike Adonijah down that same day (1 Kings 2:13-25).
